ageRange.value: All ages (highly popular for infants, toddlers, and school-age children due to walkability and outdoor focus)

extras.otherNotes: Tap water is fresh and completely drinkable. Features highly popular community-run spaces like Altspace Coworking, local organic farmer markets, and hot spring pools in nearby Banya village.

name: Cyprus (Limassol/Larnaca)
summary: Relocation-grade Israeli nesting base (~800 families Limassol/~400 Larnaca) with British/IB schools, Hebrew daycares and Chabad—year-round.

timing.bestWindow: Year-round (Relocation-grade hub with structured academic calendars)
timing.avoidWindow: July–August (Extreme Mediterranean heat often exceeding 40°C, causing many families to temporarily leave)
timing.note: Most international families operate on a year-round basis due to school enrollments. The best beach and outdoor windows are April–June and September–November.

ageRange.value: Ages 3-18 (Highly structured school systems from pre-school through secondary graduation)

priceRange.value: €4,000–€6,000 / family of 4 / month (Includes mid-range rent and private school tuition)

extras.languageOfInstruction: English (British standard curriculum) with extensive Greek and Russian options
extras.communitySize: 800-900 Israeli families in Limassol, 300-350 families in Larnaca
extras.legalVisaRisk: EU citizens have immediate residency rights. Third-Country Nationals (including Israelis, British, and Americans) must acquire structured temporary residence permits (Pink Slips) with strict proof of stable foreign income, bank deposits, and medical insurance.
extras.otherNotes: Rapidly growing Jewish/Israeli nesting infrastructure supported by six regional Chabad houses, Hebrew-speaking kindergartens, and the island's first Jewish private school scheduled to open in Limassol in 2027. All resident children qualify for the low-cost national healthcare system (GESY) once registered.

name: Goa (Arambol/Mandrem)
summary: Long-running Israeli (Arambol) and Russian (Morjim) winter-nesting coast in India with Hebrew kindergartens and beach playgroups, Nov–Mar.

timing.bestWindow: November–March (Dry winter season with fully operating beach infrastructure)
timing.avoidWindow: June–September (Monsoon season; torrential rains, structural beach closures, systemic power outages, and high risk of mosquito-borne illnesses such as Chikungunya)
timing.note: Nesting families leave Goa almost entirely outside the November–March window, as beach shacks are dismantled and the landscape transitions to heavy rainfall.

priceRange.value: ≈ ₹40,000 / month (Accommodation rent); ₹230,000–₹375,000 / year (Private international school tuition)

exactLocation.address: Arambol Beach Road, Pernem, North Goa, India, 403524

extras.languageOfInstruction: English (with Hebrew and Russian spoken inside specialized community enclaves)
extras.communitySize: Thousands of long-term nesting families and returnees each high season
extras.legalVisaRisk: Indian tourist visas impose strict maximum stay restrictions (often 90 consecutive days for many western nationals), necessitating flight runs. Foreign-owned businesses run under local nominee schemes face heavy legal penalties under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).
extras.otherNotes: Arambol features bohemian beach playgroups, yoga centers, and a relaxed, child-led environment. Morjim beach is heavily Russian-skewed and is a federally protected nesting site for endangered Olive Ridley sea turtles. Patnem (South Goa) hosts structured alternative facilities like Vidya Aranya and River House Academy; Anjuna hosts the Holistic Yellow School.
